public_rationale: The June 2024 LiveBench evaluation found Claude 3.5 Sonnet substantially ahead of other tested models in reasoning and coding [e1]. The June 2024 OlympicArena evaluation found a clear performance gap favoring GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet over Gemini 1.5 Pro and GPT-4V [e2]. These comparisons weigh against stagnation, but establish neither sustained flattening nor substantial, broad and sustained gains through April–June 2024 [e1, e2]. The evidence therefore does not settle whether capabilities were approaching a plateau [e1, e2].
limitations: The evaluations compare selected models and tasks; they do not establish the broader rate of capability improvement over successive generations.
The evidence does not supply a threshold distinguishing slowing progress from an approaching plateau.

statement.excerpt: they're allowed to get away from the very obvious problem: that Large Language Models are peaking, will not solve the kind of complex problems that actually matter, and OpenAI (and other LLM companies) are being allowed to accumulate money and power in a way that's allowed them to do actual damage in broad daylight.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that frontier LLM capability gains were approaching a plateau around publication.
Use April–June 2024, the latest completed quarter before the post, to assess the ongoing state. Earlier model generations supply comparison baselines.
Peaking does not necessarily mean that every benchmark score has stopped improving. Later breakthroughs cannot by themselves disprove this historical observation.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable independent evaluations across several capability domains show sustained flattening of frontier performance over successive model generations through the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable independent evaluations show substantial, broad and sustained frontier capability gains through the target period, inconsistent with an approaching plateau.

evidence.explanation: The June evaluation documents meaningful gains by a newly released frontier model. It weighs against a plateau, but does not establish a sustained industry-wide rate of improvement.
Another contemporary evaluation finds a performance gap favoring newer frontier models. This is counterevidence to stagnation, but a ranking snapshot cannot identify a long-term ceiling.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable evaluations across successive frontier model generations and several capability domains through June 2024, using consistent scoring and a defensible threshold to distinguish sustained flattening from substantial continuing gains.
